ch23.d.preset: Starting arrangement of the line charges
ch23.d.shape: Shape of the closed surface (drag the centre point to move it, the points on the edge to resize or reshape it)
ch23.d.view: Draw the field as field lines or grid arrows, or hide it
ch23.goal.law: Gauss' law: the electric flux through a closed surface equals the enclosed charge over $\varepsilon_0$, whatever the shape or size
ch23.goal.out: An outside charge sends as much flux in as out, so its net contribution is 0
ch23.obs.cross: Drag a charge across the surface and $\oint E_n\,dl$ jumps by that charge's $\lambda/\varepsilon_0$
ch23.obs.outside: Move an outside charge: the arrows on the surface (local $E_n$) change, the total $\oint E_n\,dl$ does not
ch23.obs.shape: Circle, square or free curve, larger or smaller: with the same charge inside, the flux is the same
ch23.obs.arrows: Arrows on the surface: the normal component $E_n$, vermilion pointing out, blue pointing in
ch23.obs.lines: Field lines: lines leaving minus lines entering the surface is proportional to the enclosed charge
ch23.obs.tray: Tray at the lower left: add or remove line charges ($\pm 1$, $\pm 2$ nC/m)
ch23.as.2d: Cross-section of infinitely long line charges perpendicular to the page. In 2D $E \propto 1/r$ and Gauss' law holds exactly; flux is per unit length
ch23.as.units: Linear charge density in nC/m, lengths in m
ch23.as.num: $\oint E_n\,dl$ is a numerical integral along the path (adaptive Simpson); $\lambda_\text{enc}$ counts each charge by how many times the path winds around it
ch23.as.snap: Charges keep at least 3.5 cm from the surface (a charge on the surface is neither inside nor outside)
